option_description: Attestation that the IdP MANDATES PKCE (S256, with code_challenge bound to code_verifier) on the authorization-code flow for ALL clients — public and confidential — and rejects /authorize requests lacking a code_challenge.
security_impact: References "Authorization code interception and replay" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when pkce_required is false (a captured authorization code can be exchanged at /token by any party because nothing binds the code to the legitimate client instance).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Proxy/inspect the /authorize request initiated by the RP and read the query parameters.
how_to_obtain.command: # Proxy/inspect the /authorize request initiated by the RP and read the query parameters
how_to_obtain.expected_output: response_type=code AND code_challenge=<43+ chars> AND code_challenge_method=S256. Absence of code_challenge or method=plain is insecure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Replay the /authorize request omitting code_challenge to prove PKCE is required, not merely accepted.
how_to_obtain.command: # Replay the /authorize request omitting code_challenge
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IdP rejects with invalid_request — proves PKCE is required, not merely accepted (defends against PKCE-downgrade).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the IdP's OpenID Connect discovery document for code_challenge_methods_supported, and inspect tenant/client policy to confirm PKCE is enforced (not merely advertised) for every registered client.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sS https://<idp_host>/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq '.code_challenge_methods_supported'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ["S256"] (no "plain"); a tenant-level setting or per-client flag confirms PKCE is mandatory for all clients.

option_description: Attestation that the IdP's /token endpoint accepts each authorization_code at most once — a second exchange returns invalid_grant and the access/refresh tokens issued from the first exchange are invalidated.
security_impact: References "Authorization code interception and replay" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when code_single_use_enforced is false (a captured code can be replayed for additional token issuance after the legitimate RP has redeemed it).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Exchange an authorization_code at /token, then immediately replay the same code and observe the response.
how_to_obtain.command: # Exchange an authorization_code at /token, then immediately replay the same code
how_to_obtain.expected_output: First exchange succeeds; second exchange returns invalid_grant. RFC 9700 recommends invalidating tokens issued from the first exchange too.

how_to_obtain.instruction: After replaying the code, attempt to call /userinfo or a protected resource with the access_token issued from the first exchange to confirm RFC 9700 §2.1.1 token-invalidation behaviour.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token_from_first_exchange>" https://<idp_host>/userinfo
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 401 invalid_token after the replay attempt — proves derived tokens were invalidated, not merely the second code rejected.

option_description: Lifetime in seconds for which the IdP will accept an authorization_code at /token after issuance. RFC 6749 §4.1.2 and RFC 9700 recommend codes be short-lived (≤60s; up to 120s tolerated).
security_impact: References "Authorization code interception and replay" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when authorization_code_ttl_seconds is greater than 120 (a lingering code gives an interception-and-replay adversary a wide window to race the legitimate RP to the token endpoint).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Exchange an authorization_code at /token to confirm single-use behaviour and observe the documented TTL.
how_to_obtain.command: # Exchange an authorization_code at /token, then immediately replay the same code
how_to_obtain.expected_output: First exchange succeeds; second exchange returns invalid_grant. RFC 9700 recommends invalidating tokens issued from the first exchange too.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Issue an /authorize request to obtain a fresh code, then wait past the documented TTL before attempting to redeem it at /token.
how_to_obtain.command: # Capture code from /authorize, sleep <ttl+10>s, then POST to /token
how_to_obtain.expected_output: /token returns invalid_grant once the TTL is exceeded — measured TTL ≤120s is acceptable; ≤60s is recommended.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the IdP tenant or realm policy that controls authorization-code lifetime (e.g. Keycloak realm token settings, Okta authorization-server policies, Auth0 tenant settings).
how_to_obtain.navigation: IdP admin console -> Realm/Tenant settings -> Tokens -> 'Authorization code lifespan' (or vendor equivalent)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configured value is ≤60s (recommended) or at worst ≤120s.

option_description: Attestation that the IdP enforces code_challenge_method=S256 on every /authorize request and rejects requests that omit code_challenge or present a non-S256 method.
security_impact: References "PKCE downgrade attack" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when pkce_method_s256_required is false (an active MITM can coerce the client into omitting PKCE or falling back to plain, turning an eavesdropped code_challenge into a usable code_verifier — RFC 7636 §7.2).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Send an /authorize request with code_challenge_method=plain and confirm the IdP rejects it.
how_to_obtain.command: # Send an /authorize request with code_challenge_method=plain
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IdP rejects (invalid_request) — only S256 is honoured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the IdP discovery document and confirm code_challenge_methods_supported lists S256 only.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sS https://<idp_host>/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq '.code_challenge_methods_supported'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ["S256"] — "plain" must not be advertised or accepted.

option_description: Attestation that the IdP accepts code_challenge_method=plain (or silently falls back to plain when S256 verification fails) on the authorization endpoint.
security_impact: References "PKCE downgrade attack" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when code_challenge_method_plain_accepted is true (an eavesdropper on the front channel can reuse the challenge as the verifier at /token, defeating the PKCE binding between the client instance and the authorization code).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Send an /authorize request with code_challenge_method=plain to determine whether the IdP accepts it.
how_to_obtain.command: # Send an /authorize request with code_challenge_method=plain
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IdP rejects (invalid_request) — only S256 is honoured. If the IdP issues a code, complete the exchange at /token using the challenge value as the verifier — if /token accepts, plain is silently honoured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe for silent fallback: send /authorize with a malformed S256 challenge and watch whether the IdP downgrades to plain validation at /token.
how_to_obtain.command: # /authorize with code_challenge=<short> and code_challenge_method=S256, then /token with code_verifier equal to code_challenge
how_to_obtain.expected_output: /token rejects (invalid_grant) — confirms no silent plain fallback. Acceptance signals a downgrade window.

option_description: Attestation that the RP generates a per-session nonce, includes it in the /authorize request, AND verifies on callback that the same value is echoed in the id_token's nonce claim.
security_impact: References "ID Token replay via missing or unchecked nonce" — its sole OR-condition — firing when oidc_nonce_validated is false (a captured ID Token can be replayed across user-agent sessions; see GHSA-3gx8-q682-38mx where nonce was generated but never compared).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture an /authorize request then decode the returned id_token and inspect the nonce claim.
how_to_obtain.command: # Capture /authorize then decode the returned id_token and inspect the nonce claim
how_to_obtain.expected_output: id_token.nonce equals the value sent in /authorize. Replaying a previously-used id_token MUST be rejected by the RP.
how_to_obtain.source: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §3.1.2.1, §3.1.3.7; GHSA-3gx8-q682-38mx (roadiz nonce-never-validated advisory)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect RP source code or framework configuration to confirm BOTH nonce generation per /authorize AND comparison on id_token receipt are wired up (the common bug is generation without verification).
how_to_obtain.command: grep -RInE '(nonce|id_token)' <rp_codebase>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Both nonce write (on /authorize build) and nonce read+compare (on /callback id_token parse) are present in the auth handler.

option_description: Attestation that the RP generates a high-entropy per-request `state` value on /authorize, binds it to the user-agent session (cookie or server-side store), and verifies it byte-for-byte on /callback before accepting the authorization response.
security_impact: References "Login CSRF via missing or unbound state parameter" — its sole OR-condition — firing when oauth_state_bound_and_verified is false (the authentication-response leg is unbound from the initiating session, enabling login-CSRF and session-fixation as called out in RFC 6749 §10.12).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture two consecutive /authorize requests and tamper with the state on /callback to observe the RP's behaviour.
how_to_obtain.command: # Capture two consecutive /authorize requests and the /callback handler behaviour
how_to_obtain.expected_output: `state` differs across requests, is >=128 bits of entropy, and tampering with it on /callback causes the RP to reject the response.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 6749 §10.12; RFC 9700 §4.7; OWASP CSRF Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Issue a /callback from a different browser session (no matching session cookie) carrying a valid-for-elsewhere state and confirm the RP rejects it (session binding, not just value comparison).
how_to_obtain.command: # Replay /callback?code=...&state=... in a fresh session with no matching cookie
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RP rejects — state is bound to the session-store key, not merely echoed.

option_description: Attestation that the IdP matches the inbound redirect_uri against the registered allowlist using exact byte-for-byte string comparison — no wildcards, no regex, no path-prefix, no scheme/host normalisation (localhost ports for native apps excepted).
security_impact: References "redirect_uri pattern-match / open-redirect exploit" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when redirect_uri_exact_match_enforced is false (pattern matching lets the attacker steer the authorization response to an attacker origin and capture the code or fragment-mode token — RFC 9700 §2.1.3).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Send /authorize with redirect_uri variants (trailing slash, fragment, extra path, attacker-controlled subdomain) and confirm each is rejected.
how_to_obtain.command: # Send /authorize with redirect_uri that differs by a trailing slash, fragment, extra path, or attacker-controlled subdomain
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IdP rejects with invalid_request/invalid_redirect_uri for every variant that is not byte-identical to a registered URI.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the IdP client-registration entry to confirm only exact HTTPS URIs are registered (no `*`, no regex anchors, no path-prefix templates).
how_to_obtain.navigation: IdP admin console -> Clients -> <client_id> -> 'Allowed Callback URLs' / 'Valid Redirect URIs'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: List contains only literal https:// URIs that the RP actually uses; no wildcard or pattern entries.

option_description: Attestation that the RP validates post-login returnTo / RelayState / continue parameters against a server-side allowlist of internal paths, refusing to redirect off-origin.
security_impact: References "redirect_uri pattern-match / open-redirect exploit" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when post_login_returnto_allowlisted is false (the authentication response leg is weaponised to phish users or leak codes via Referer — RFC 9700 §4.10).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Send a login URL with a returnTo pointing at an external origin and observe whether the RP follows it after authentication.
how_to_obtain.command: # Send a login URL with ?returnTo=https://attacker.example/
how_to_obtain.expected_output: After auth, the RP refuses to redirect off-origin; redirects only to allowlisted internal paths.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Unvalidated Redirects Cheat Sheet; RFC 9700 §4.10

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the RP codebase for the returnTo / RelayState / continue handler to confirm it validates against a server-side allowlist (not regex on hostname, which is bypassable).
how_to_obtain.command: grep -RInE '(returnTo|RelayState|continue|next)\s*=' <rp_codebase>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Handler resolves the supplied value against a static list of internal paths, or rejects any value with a scheme/authority component.

option_description: Attestation that the SP verifies the IdP's XML-DSig signature on the SAML Assertion (and ideally the Response) using a pinned IdP certificate, with signature-wrapping defences (canonicalisation + reference validation rejecting wrapped/duplicate Assertions).
security_impact: References "SAML signature wrapping, replay, and audience confusion" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when saml_assertion_signature_verified is false (full SP impersonation via tampered SAMLResponse — see CVE-2022-23607, CVE-2024-45409).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Submit unsigned and signature-wrapping variants of a SAMLResponse to the SP's ACS endpoint and confirm rejection.
how_to_obtain.command: # Submit a SAMLResponse with a tampered Assertion, a stale NotOnOrAfter, a different AudienceRestriction, and a replayed AssertionID
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SP rejects all four. XML signature-wrapping variants are also rejected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the SAML toolkit version in use carries fixes for XML signature-wrapping CVEs (CVE-2022-23607 python-saml; CVE-2024-45409 ruby-saml) and that the IdP signing certificate is pinned, not 'trust anything signed'.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SP SAML config -> 'IdP Certificate' / 'Signing Cert' — confirm a fingerprint or PEM, not a CA bundle reference
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Toolkit version is on the patched line; signing cert is pinned by fingerprint or PEM.

option_description: Attestation that the SP enforces Conditions/AudienceRestriction by exact match against its own EntityID (no wildcards, no prefix match) and rejects assertions issued for a different audience.
security_impact: References "SAML signature wrapping, replay, and audience confusion" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when saml_audience_restriction_strict is false (cross-SP assertion confusion: an assertion legitimately issued for SP-A is accepted by SP-B).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Submit a SAMLResponse whose AudienceRestriction names a different SP's EntityID and confirm rejection.
how_to_obtain.command: # Submit a SAMLResponse with a tampered Assertion, a stale NotOnOrAfter, a different AudienceRestriction, and a replayed AssertionID
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SP rejects all four. XML signature-wrapping variants are also rejected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the SP's expected Audience / EntityID configuration and confirm it is a literal string the SP compares byte-for-byte (not a regex or prefix).
how_to_obtain.navigation: SP SAML config -> 'EntityID' / 'Audience' — compare to the value in incoming Assertions' <AudienceRestriction>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Single literal EntityID configured; comparison is exact-match.

option_description: Attestation that the SP validates SubjectConfirmationData.Recipient against its own ACS URL and SubjectConfirmationData.InResponseTo against an AuthnRequest ID the SP actually issued.
security_impact: References "SAML signature wrapping, replay, and audience confusion" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when saml_recipient_inresponseto_matched is false (unsolicited or cross-endpoint assertion injection succeeds).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inject an unsolicited assertion (no prior AuthnRequest) and a separate assertion whose Recipient is a different ACS URL; confirm both rejected.
how_to_obtain.command: # Submit a SAMLResponse with a tampered Assertion, a stale NotOnOrAfter, a different AudienceRestriction, and a replayed AssertionID
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SP rejects all four. XML signature-wrapping variants are also rejected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the SP records issued AuthnRequest IDs in a server-side store and rejects responses whose InResponseTo is unknown or already-consumed.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SP source / config -> 'AuthnRequest cache' / 'InResponseTo store' (e.g. session store or short-lived KV)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: InResponseTo is matched against a stored request ID; unsolicited assertions are either rejected or governed by an explicit IdP-initiated-SSO toggle that is OFF by default.

option_description: Attestation that the SP maintains a seen-AssertionID cache for the validity window (NotBefore..NotOnOrAfter) and rejects any AssertionID it has already consumed.
security_impact: References "SAML signature wrapping, replay, and audience confusion" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when saml_assertion_replay_cache_active is false (a still-valid Assertion can be replayed within its lifetime).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Consume a SAML Assertion successfully, then resubmit the identical (still-valid) Assertion to the SP's ACS and confirm rejection on the second submission.
how_to_obtain.command: # Submit a SAMLResponse with a tampered Assertion, a stale NotOnOrAfter, a different AudienceRestriction, and a replayed AssertionID
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SP rejects all four. XML signature-wrapping variants are also rejected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the SP's SAML toolkit configuration enables the AssertionID replay cache with a TTL at least as long as the maximum NotOnOrAfter window.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SP SAML config -> 'OneTimeUse' / 'Replay cache' / 'Assertion ID cache TTL'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Replay cache enabled, TTL ≥ assertion validity window.

option_description: Attestation that the IdP enforces a phishing-resistant authenticator (WebAuthn/FIDO2, smartcard) on the authentication handshake — origin-bound credentials an Evilginx-class reverse-proxy phishing kit cannot relay.
security_impact: References "Phishing-driven MFA bypass via AiTM reverse proxy" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when phishing_resistant_authenticator_required is false (an AiTM proxy can pass password + OTP/push through in real time and harvest the resulting session — NIST SP 800-63B AAL2/AAL3).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt login as a privileged user with only a password and observe the authentication policy enforcement.
how_to_obtain.command: Attempt login as a privileged user with only password
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Login fails / second-factor challenge is mandatory. Bypass via legacy endpoint is also blocked.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-63B Rev 4 §4.2-4.3; OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the IdP conditional-access / MFA policy for coverage gaps and confirm WebAuthn/FIDO2 (or smartcard) is the required factor, with password+OTP/push fallback disabled for the user population in scope.
how_to_obtain.command: # Review the IdP conditional-access / MFA policy for coverage gaps (service accounts, legacy protocols, IP allowlist bypasses)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No identity class exempt from MFA except documented break-glass, which itself has compensating controls. Required authenticator class is phishing-resistant (WebAuthn/FIDO2 or smartcard).

option_description: Attestation that access tokens (and where supported, session cookies) issued on the handshake are sender-constrained — mTLS-bound (RFC 8705, cnf.x5t#S256) or DPoP-bound (RFC 9449, cnf.jkt) — so a token harvested by an AiTM proxy, XSS, log leak, or malicious browser extension cannot be replayed from a different sender.
security_impact: References both "Phishing-driven MFA bypass via AiTM reverse proxy" (one of its OR-conditions, firing when sender_constrained is false) and "Bearer access token theft and replay from a different sender" (one of its OR-conditions, firing when sender_constrained is false) — without proof-of-possession (mTLS x5t#S256 or DPoP jkt cnf claim) plain bearer tokens are usable from any sender once stolen.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Decode an access_token (if JWT) and check for a cnf claim; or read the token-endpoint response for token_type.
how_to_obtain.command: # Decode an access_token (if JWT) and check for cnf claim; or read the token-endpoint response for token_type
how_to_obtain.expected_output: token_type=DPoP or the JWT contains a `cnf` claim (jkt or x5t#S256). Plain `Bearer` with no binding is the insecure case.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Replay a captured access_token from a different client / different DPoP key / different mTLS client cert and confirm rejection.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <stolen_token>" https://<rs_host>/api/resource
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Resource server returns 401 invalid_token (or invalid_dpop_proof) when the proof-of-possession does not match — confirms binding is enforced, not merely advertised.

option_description: Attestation that the authentication endpoint enforces per-account AND per-IP throttling with progressive delay, CAPTCHA escalation, or temporary lockout on repeated failures (per-IP alone is defeated by botnets).
security_impact: References "Credential stuffing and online brute force" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when rate_limiting_or_lockout_enabled is false (mass replay of breached credential pairs or password guessing against privileged accounts becomes feasible — NIST SP 800-63B §5.2.2).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Issue many failed login attempts against a test account from a single IP, then from many IPs, to confirm both per-account and per-IP throttling fire.
how_to_obtain.command: # Issue 100+ failed login attempts against a test account from one IP, then from many IPs
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Per-account throttling triggers (responses slow / 429 / CAPTCHA / temp-lock) regardless of source IP diversity.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-63B Rev 4 §5.2.2; OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the IdP brute-force / detection-policy configuration to confirm both per-account and per-IP keys are armed, with thresholds tuned to avoid trivial DoS-by-lockout.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IdP admin console -> Security -> 'Brute Force Protection' / 'Detections' / 'Sign-in risk policy'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Both per-account and per-IP throttles are enabled; thresholds documented; ~100-attempt ceiling per NIST.

option_description: Attestation that the authentication flow screens submitted (and newly chosen) passwords against a known-breached-credentials corpus (e.g. HaveIBeenPwned k-anonymity API, NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1.2 compromised-credentials check) and rejects or steps-up on a hit.
security_impact: References "Credential stuffing and online brute force" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when breached_password_screening_enabled is false (previously-leaked credential pairs remain usable, the precise attack credential-stuffing automates).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt to set or log in with a known-pwned password (e.g. 'P@ssw0rd') and observe the response.
how_to_obtain.command: # Attempt to set / log in with a known-pwned password (e.g. 'P@ssw0rd')
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rejected at set-time, or step-up challenged / blocked at sign-in.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the IdP password policy enables a compromised-credentials check (HaveIBeenPwned k-anonymity, or vendor equivalent) for both registration/change AND sign-in paths.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IdP admin console -> Authentication -> Password Policy -> 'Check against breached passwords' / 'Compromised credentials'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Feature enabled for both set-password and sign-in flows.

option_description: Attestation that secrets (passwords, authorization codes, ID/access tokens, SAMLResponse) are carried in URL path or query string on this flow. The secure value is false — secrets MUST be in request bodies or headers.
security_impact: References "Secrets in URL leaking via Referer, logs, and browser history" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when transmitted_in_url_or_query is true (URL-borne secrets end up in proxy/access logs, Referer headers to third-party origins, and shared browser history — RFC 9700 §4.3).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep web access logs for secret-bearing query parameters.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E '(password=|access_token=|id_token=|code=|SAMLResponse=)' <web_access_log>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No hits. Any hit is a sensitive-data-in-URL leak (becomes a Referer leak too).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP ASVS V9 / Authentication Cheat Sheet; RFC 9700 §4.3

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture the handshake traffic (intercepting proxy or tcpdump+TLS-keys) and inspect every URL path/query for token/code/password material.
how_to_obtain.command: # mitmproxy / Burp on the browser <-> IdP and browser <-> RP legs; export URLs and grep
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No secret material in any URL — codes/tokens appear only in POST bodies or Authorization headers.

option_description: Attestation that any secret material that traverses this flow is masked/redacted in proxy, gateway, and application access logs (and excluded from Referer propagation).
security_impact: References "Secrets in URL leaking via Referer, logs, and browser history" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when secrets_masked_in_logs is false (even header/body-borne secrets leak via log retention and downstream analytics when unmasked).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review IdP and RP logging config for token-scrubbing on Authorization headers and form bodies.
how_to_obtain.command: # Review IdP and RP logging config for token-scrubbing on Authorization headers and form bodies
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Authorization headers and password/token form fields are redacted before write.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Trigger a handshake with a marker token value and grep proxy, gateway, app, and SIEM logs for the marker.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -RIn '<marker_token_value>' <log_directories>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No hits — the marker appears only as '***' / '[REDACTED]' / a truncated digest. Plain marker presence anywhere in the log chain is a finding.

option_description: Time-to-live of access tokens issued on this authentication flow, in minutes. RFC 9700 recommends short-lived access tokens (commonly ≤60 minutes) paired with refresh-token rotation.
security_impact: References "Bearer access token theft and replay from a different sender" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when access_token_ttl_minutes is greater than 60 (long-lived unbound bearer tokens dramatically widen the replay window after theft).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Decode an issued access_token (if JWT) and compute exp − iat in minutes; otherwise read the token-endpoint expires_in field.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sS -X POST https://<idp_host>/token -d 'grant_type=...' | jq '.expires_in' # then divide by 60
how_to_obtain.expected_output: expires_in ≤ 3600 (≤60 minutes). For JWT tokens, (exp − iat)/60 ≤ 60.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect IdP token-lifetime policy for the access-token TTL applied to clients on this flow.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IdP admin console -> Token settings (per realm, tenant, or authorization-server) -> 'Access token lifespan'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configured access-token lifespan ≤60 minutes; longer-lived needs documented refresh-token rotation justification.
